title: Sorting and ranking
summary: sort_values on several columns, the top rows per group, rank, value_counts and idxmax.
hints: `leaderboard`: `df.sort_values(["score", "minutes", "name"], ascending=[False, True, True]).reset_index(drop=True)`: one `ascending` flag per column.

`top_n_per_class`: sort first (`["cls", "score", "name"]` with `ascending=[True, False, True]`), then `.groupby("cls").head(n)` keeps the first `n` rows of each class in the sorted order; finish with `reset_index(drop=True)`.

`add_rank`: `df["score"].rank(method="dense", ascending=False).astype(int)`; "dense" gives ties the same rank with no gaps (1, 2, 2, 3). `class_counts`: `df["cls"].value_counts()` then a dict of plain ints. `best_student`: `df.loc[df["score"].idxmax(), "name"]`.
